title: Asking About the Weather: Milyen az idő?

sections.title: Milyen az idő?
sections.content: Milyen az idő? ("What's the weather like?") reuses the milyen question you already know from describing people and places. The short answer pattern is just an adjective plus van: Szép idő van. ("The weather is nice.", literally "nice weather is [there]"). Hungarian doesn't need a separate word for "it" here — the weather adjective and van carry the whole sentence.

items.spanish: Szép idő van, napos és meleg.
items.english: The weather is nice, sunny and warm.

items.spanish: Ma felhős és szeles idő van.

sections.content: napos, felhős and szeles are all built with the same -s ending you already know from describing people ("having X") — felhő ("cloud") + -s = felhős ("having clouds" = cloudy). Once you spot the pattern, new weather words are easy to guess.
